thread:
Jen L: FYI customer ACME just escalated — after last night's canary they see different rerank top-1 for identical payloads. attached sample pair.
Marco P: Ugh. Do we have a canary note? which model variant?
Jen L: rerank-v2-3 canary, 10% at ~02:14 UTC per deploy-bot. Customer pasted two responses (old vs new) and scores:
Jen L: ```json
{"query":"return policy","cands":["30-day refund","no refunds after 14 days","refund exceptions"]}
old_scores: [0.87,0.08,0.05]
new_scores: [0.32,0.61,0.07]
``` 
Jen L: They validated inputs are byte-for-byte identical and hashed them in their CI.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary started rerank-v2-3 @ 2026-03-04T02:14:11Z -> 10% traffic
Anita R: quick hypothesis: tokenization/truncation defaults changed in the new tokenizer build. We flipped a config during tokenfast upgrade (v2.0 -> v2.1) to trim_long_sequences='end' to keep prefixes, thought it would be safe.
Samir K: I reproduced locally. With tokenfast v2.0 tokenizer we get old_scores; with v2.1 we get new_scores. The diff is from how punctuation and leading whitespace are tokenized — candidate ranking is sensitive to a 1-2 token shift in some templates.
Samir K: repro steps I ran:
Samir K: ```bash
# use same model weights pinned to rerank-v2-3
python -m tools/rerank_repro --model rerank-v2-3 --tokenizer tokenfast@v2.1 --payload samples/acme_query.json
python -m tools/rerank_repro --model rerank-v2-3 --tokenizer tokenfast@v2.0 --payload samples/acme_query.json
```
Samir K: results show score divergence matching ACME's dump.
Marco P: did we change padding/truncation defaults anywhere else? maybe a global config in serving runtime.
Anita R: we also changed default max_input_tokens from 2048->4096 in the model manifest for v2-3 (to support longer contexts) and enabled aggressive prefix caching. that plus different trimming strategy explains occasional 413s customers reported after forcing long inputs, but not in this case.
Jen L: ACME said they haven't sent longer inputs, they run canonical short queries. so the tokenization shift is the likely cause.
Samir K: short-term mitigation: we can gate canary traffic to fallback tokenization path. patch idea: force tokenizer override to tokenfast@v2.0 in the router for canary until we vet.
Jen L: action: roll canary back to tokenfast v2.0 for rerank-v2-3 and notify ACME. I'll coordinate with platform ops.
Marco P: test coverage: add deterministic tokenization checks to CI: take a small set of canonical queries, run both tokenizers and assert identical token sequences for supported inputs or explicitly accept deltas and warn.
Anita R: long-term: add tokenizer-version pinning in model manifest and surface tokenizer diff warnings in the Console on model upload. also add a regression eval that compares rerank A/B on a kept prompt set.
Samir K: logging note: we should log tokenizer version/hash per request (add to trace headers) so customers and us can tie outputs to tokenizer code.
ops-bot: infra: created incident-1715-ticket for "rerank tokenization delta after tokenizer upgrade" and assigned to eng-ml.
Jen L: I'll reply to customer: "we found a tokenizer upgrade in canary causing token shifts; rolling canary back to previous tokenizer and will follow up with regression details + timeline." :white_check_mark:
Marco P: thanks — keep me posted if rollback doesn't fully reproduce the customer's numbers.
Samir K: follow-up tasks I took: run corpus-wide rerank diff on our regression set, add tokenization diff assert, prepare rollout plan to reintroduce tokenfast v2.1 with compatibility tests.
Jen L: timeline: rollback start in 10m, pinged ops, will update thread when done.
